static_analysis.title: Unclosed file handle and no error handling on config load
static_analysis.description: CONFIG is loaded via json.load(open('config.json')) without closing the file handle and without any try/except. If the file is missing or malformed, the entire module fails to import with an unhandled exception, crashing the application at startup.

static_analysis.title: Hardcoded fallback secret key
static_analysis.description: SECRET_KEY falls back to the literal string 'hardcoded-fallback-secret-123' if the config key is absent. Any deployment where config.json omits 'secret_key' silently uses a publicly known, trivially guessable secret.

static_analysis.title: SQL injection in get_price via f-string query
static_analysis.description: The SKU value from external input is interpolated directly into a SQL string. An attacker-controlled SKU can break out of the string literal, inject arbitrary SQL, and read, modify, or delete data.
static_analysis.suggested_fix: price = self.db.query('SELECT price FROM products WHERE sku = %s', (sku,))

static_analysis.title: SQL injection in _save_order via f-string INSERT
static_analysis.description: order['id'], order['user_id'], and order['total'] are interpolated directly into an INSERT statement. This is also executed outside a transaction with no rollback capability.
static_analysis.suggested_fix:
with self.db.transaction():
    self.db.execute(
        'INSERT INTO orders (id, user_id, total) VALUES (%s, %s, %s)',
        (order['id'], order['user_id'], order['total'])
    )

static_analysis.title: Plaintext password storage
static_analysis.description: In UserManager.create_user, the password is stored as-is. The authenticate method also compares in plaintext. A DB dump immediately exposes all user passwords.
static_analysis.suggested_fix:
import bcrypt
hashed = bcrypt.hashpw(password.encode(), bcrypt.gensalt())
user['password'] = hashed
# In authenticate:
bcrypt.checkpw(password.encode(), user['password'])

static_analysis.title: MD5 used for order ID generation
static_analysis.description: MD5 is cryptographically broken, and timestamp-seeded IDs are predictable and not collision-resistant under high load, making order IDs guessable.
static_analysis.suggested_fix:
import uuid
return str(uuid.uuid4())

static_analysis.title: KeyError on missing order_data fields with no input validation
static_analysis.description: process_order directly accesses order_data['user_id'] and order_data['items'] without any validation. Missing keys propagate as raw KeyError with no context.
static_analysis.suggested_fix:
if 'user_id' not in order_data or 'items' not in order_data:
    raise ValueError('order_data must contain user_id and items')

static_analysis.title: Magic number for discount threshold and rate
static_analysis.description: The values 1000 and 0.9 appear as bare literals with no named constant or documentation.
static_analysis.suggested_fix:
DISCOUNT_THRESHOLD = 1000
DISCOUNT_MULTIPLIER = 0.9

static_analysis.title: get_all_orders exposes mutable internal list
static_analysis.description: Returns a direct reference to self.orders. Any caller that mutates the returned list silently corrupts the processor's internal state.
static_analysis.suggested_fix: return list(self.orders)

static_analysis.title: cancel_order does not persist cancellation to database
static_analysis.description: The method updates the in-memory status to 'cancelled' but never issues a corresponding UPDATE to the database. Cancellation is lost after process restart.
static_analysis.suggested_fix: self.db.execute('UPDATE orders SET status = %s WHERE id = %s', ('cancelled', order_id))

static_analysis.title: calculate_tax returns None for unknown country
static_analysis.description: The if/elif chain has no else or default return. For any country code not in {US, UK, DE}, the function returns None implicitly. Callers using the result arithmetically will receive a TypeError.
static_analysis.suggested_fix:
else:
    raise ValueError(f'Tax rate not defined for country: {country}')

static_analysis.title: Non-unique user ID generation
static_analysis.description: User IDs are assigned as len(self.users) + 1. If any user is ever deleted, the next insertion can produce an ID already assigned to a previous user.
static_analysis.suggested_fix:
Use a monotonically incrementing counter:
self._next_id = 1
user['id'] = self._next_id
self._next_id += 1

static_analysis.title: bulk_import_orders opens file without context manager or encoding
static_analysis.description: open(file_path).read() leaks the file handle and specifies no encoding. On Windows the default encoding may silently corrupt non-ASCII data.
static_analysis.suggested_fix:
with open(file_path, encoding='utf-8') as f:
    data = f.read()

static_analysis.title: Fragile CSV parsing does not handle quoted fields or errors
static_analysis.description: Manual split(',') does not handle RFC 4180 quoted fields or embedded commas. parts[2] accessed without bounds checking will raise IndexError on short lines.
static_analysis.suggested_fix:
import csv
with open(file_path, encoding='utf-8', newline='') as f:
    reader = csv.DictReader(f)
    for row in reader:
        ...

static_analysis.title: String-based date comparison is fragile and incorrect
static_analysis.description: created_at is stored as str(datetime.datetime.now()) and compared lexicographically. Mixed formats or timezone differences produce wrong results silently.

static_analysis.title: print used instead of logger for email notification
static_analysis.description: print() output is invisible in log aggregation systems, cannot be filtered by level, and provides no timestamps or context.
static_analysis.suggested_fix: logger.info('Sending email to user %s for order %s', user_id, order['id'])

static_analysis.title: String concatenation for message building instead of f-string
static_analysis.description: The notification message is built with multiple + concatenations and str() casts.
static_analysis.suggested_fix: msg = f"Dear user {user_id}, your order {order['id']} total is ${order['total']:.2f}"

static_analysis.title: O(n) linear scan in get_user instead of indexed lookup
static_analysis.description: UserManager stores users keyed by username but get_user searches by ID via full iteration. As user count grows this becomes increasingly expensive.
static_analysis.suggested_fix: Maintain a secondary dict keyed by user ID: self._users_by_id = {}

static_analysis.title: generate_report loads all orders into memory
static_analysis.description: The function retrieves all orders in-memory and filters them. For large datasets this is a scalability problem.
static_analysis.suggested_fix:
Push filtering to the database:
db.query('SELECT * FROM orders WHERE created_at BETWEEN %s AND %s', (start_date, end_date))

static_analysis.title: Overly permissive email validation regex
static_analysis.description: The regex r'.+@.+' matches any string with an @ surrounded by at least one character, accepting 'a@b', '@@@', or 'x@y@z'.
static_analysis.suggested_fix:
EMAIL_RE = re.compile(r'^[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[\w.]+$')
return bool(EMAIL_RE.match(email))

static_analysis.title: chunk raises ZeroDivisionError when size is 0
static_analysis.description: chunk(lst, 0) passes size=0 to range(0, len(lst), 0), which raises ValueError. No guard exists.
static_analysis.suggested_fix:
if size <= 0:
    raise ValueError(f'chunk size must be a positive integer, got {size}')

static_analysis.title: sanitize_input only strips whitespace — not a real sanitizer
static_analysis.description: The function only calls str(value).strip(). It performs no escaping, HTML encoding, SQL metacharacter removal, or length limiting. Callers may believe input is safe and skip further validation.
static_analysis.suggested_fix: Rename to normalize_whitespace() to avoid false confidence, or implement context-appropriate sanitization.

static_analysis.title: Dead code: _legacy_format_price is never called
static_analysis.description: _legacy_format_price is defined but never referenced anywhere. Dead code increases cognitive load.
static_analysis.suggested_fix: Remove the function.

static_analysis.title: retry has fixed sleep interval and catches bare Exception
static_analysis.description: retry catches bare Exception (too broad), logs nothing on intermediate failures, and always sleeps exactly 1 second. Transient vs permanent errors are indistinguishable.
static_analysis.suggested_fix: Add exponential backoff, specific exception types, and warning logging on each retry attempt.

risk_assessment.reason: Central orchestrator with no error handling or rollback. Any dependency failure silently corrupts state.
SQL injection + db=None crash at construction time.
Module-level open() crashes entire module on import if config.json missing.
Plaintext passwords, non-unique IDs under deletions.
Plaintext comparison. Tightly coupled to create_user.
One bad CSV row aborts entire batch. No per-row error isolation.
Returns None for unknown countries — causes TypeError in arithmetic callers.
Always returns empty list (instantiates fresh OrderProcessor). String date comparison is fragile.
No DB write, no user notification. In-memory and DB diverge.
Returns internal mutable list — external mutation corrupts state.

new_test_suggestions.test_description: Verify order with total <= 1000 is processed without a discount.
new_test_suggestions.test_template:
def test_process_order_no_discount(mocker):
    processor = OrderProcessor()
    mocker.patch.object(processor, 'get_price', return_value=10.0)
    mocker.patch.object(processor, '_save_order')
    mocker.patch.object(processor, '_notify_user')
    result = processor.process_order({'user_id': 'u1', 'items': [{'sku': 'SKU1', 'qty': 5}]})
    assert result['total'] == 50.0
    assert result['status'] == 'pending'

new_test_suggestions.test_description: Verify 10% discount applied when raw total > 1000.
new_test_suggestions.test_template:
def test_process_order_applies_discount_when_total_exceeds_1000(mocker):
    processor = OrderProcessor()
    mocker.patch.object(processor, 'get_price', return_value=200.0)
    mocker.patch.object(processor, '_save_order')
    mocker.patch.object(processor, '_notify_user')
    result = processor.process_order({'user_id': 'u2', 'items': [{'sku': 'SKU2', 'qty': 6}]})
    assert result['total'] == pytest.approx(200.0 * 6 * 0.9)

def test_create_user_returns_expected_fields():

    user = manager.create_user('alice', 'secret', 'alice@example.com')
    assert user['username'] == 'alice'

    result = manager.authenticate('alice', 'secret')

def test_bulk_import_orders_valid_csv(mocker, tmp_path):
    csv_file = tmp_path / 'orders.csv'
    csv_file.write_text('u1,SKU1,2\nu2,SKU2,3\n')
    mocker.patch('app.OrderProcessor.get_price', return_value=10.0)
    mocker.patch('app.OrderProcessor._save_order')
    mocker.patch('app.OrderProcessor._notify_user')
    from app import bulk_import_orders
    results = bulk_import_orders(str(csv_file))
    assert len(results) == 2

def test_bulk_import_orders_file_not_found():
    from app import bulk_import_orders
    with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
        bulk_import_orders('/nonexistent/orders.csv')

def test_generate_report_filters_by_date_range(mocker):

    mock_orders = [
        {'id': '1', 'created_at': '2024-01-10', 'total': 100},
        {'id': '2', 'created_at': '2024-02-15', 'total': 200},
        {'id': '3', 'created_at': '2024-03-20', 'total': 300},
    ]
    mocker.patch('app.OrderProcessor.get_all_orders', return_value=mock_orders)
    result = generate_report('2024-01-01', '2024-02-28')
    assert len(result) == 2
